speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Welcome to Northstar Insurance's lifecycle modeling workshop. We will build one coherent model from product ideation through sale, bind, issuance, servicing, billing, and renewal.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: We will finish one sub-domain before touching the next. In every pass we will identify events first, then commands and actors, then hotspots, then policies and invariants, and finally the screens people need.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Our product is a digital Business Owners Policy for independent retailers and professional offices with less than five million dollars in annual revenue.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain one is Product Design. Events only for now: what business facts tell the story from opportunity to an approved product design?

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Market Opportunity Identified is first, followed by Product Concept Proposed and Target Segment Selected.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Then Exposure Assumptions Defined, Expected Loss Model Completed, and Indicated Rate Developed.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Coverage Package Designed, Eligibility Strategy Defined, and Risk Appetite Defined describe the underwriting side of the design.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Consumer Disclosure Requirements Identified and Product Design Approved complete the internal design sequence.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Event sequence confirmed: opportunity, concept, segment, exposure assumptions, loss model, indicated rate, coverage, eligibility strategy, risk appetite, disclosures, and internal approval.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors for Product Design.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: A Product Manager issues Research Market Opportunity, Propose Product Concept, Select Target Segment, and Design Coverage Package.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: An Actuary issues Define Exposure Assumptions, Model Expected Losses, and Develop Indicated Rate.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: A Product Underwriter issues Define Eligibility Strategy and Define Risk Appetite.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: A Compliance Analyst issues Identify Disclosure Requirements, and the Product Committee issues Approve Product Design.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Product Design hotspots. What could make this model ambiguous or unsafe?

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Hotspot: Product and Underwriting use eligibility differently. Product means target market; Underwriting means an executable acceptance gate.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Resolution: Product Design owns Eligibility Strategy as intent. Underwriting Decisioning later owns executable Eligibility Rules.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Hotspot: an indicated rate can change while coverage design is still moving, so a rate can be paired with the wrong assumptions.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: every Expected Loss Model and Indicated Rate references the immutable Product Design Version it evaluated.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Product Design policies and invariants.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Policy: whenever the target segment or coverage package changes materially, the loss model and indicated rate return to review.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Policy: Product Design Approved only when coverage, appetite intent, indicated rate, disclosures, profitability target, and accountable owners are present.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Invariant: one Product Design Version contains one internally consistent set of coverage definitions, exposure assumptions, and indicated rates.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Finally Product Design screens and read models.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Product Portfolio Roadmap shows concepts, target segments, design versions, approval state, target launch, and accountable Product Manager.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Rate Indication Workbench shows assumptions, expected losses, expenses, trend, credibility, indicated rate, and linked design version.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Product Design Review shows coverage, eligibility strategy, appetite intent, unresolved decisions, and approval evidence.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Product Design is coherent. Its output is Product Design Approved with an immutable version. We now move to Regulatory Filing.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain two is Regulatory Filing. Events first: what happens from an approved design to legal availability?

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Filing Package Prepared, Filing Submitted, Filing Acknowledged, and Regulatory Review Started.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: The review can produce Filing Question Received or Filing Objection Received.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Responses may lead to Filing Package Revised and Rate Filing Revised.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: The terminal facts are Filing Approved, Filing Disapproved, or Filing Withdrawn. For approved filings, Approved Effective Date Recorded follows.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: A Filing Analyst issues Prepare Filing Package, Submit Filing, Answer Regulatory Question, Respond to Filing Objection, Revise Filing Package, and Withdraw Filing.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: An Actuary issues Revise Rate Filing when the response changes a factor, assumption, or actuarial memorandum.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: A Product Manager issues Accept Approved Effective Date or Request Later Launch Date. We cannot sell merely because approval arrived.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Regulatory Filing hotspots.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Hotspot: approval is jurisdiction-specific. Saying Product Approved without a state and effective date is dangerously vague.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: Filing Approved always identifies jurisdiction, approved product version, approved rate version, forms, conditions, and earliest effective date.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Hotspot: a filing response may alter rates without Product realizing the commercial proposition changed.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Resolution: material Filing Package Revised events trigger Product Design Impact Review before the response is finalized.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Regulatory Filing policies and invariants.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Policy: whenever Filing Question Received or Filing Objection Received, assign an owner and due date and place the filing in Response Required.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Policy: only Filing Approved plus Approved Effective Date Recorded can create Jurisdiction Authorized for Sale.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Invariant: every quoted jurisdiction must resolve to exactly one approved combination of product, rate, form, and disclosure versions for the requested effective date.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Regulatory Filing screens.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Filing Tracker shows jurisdiction, filing number, submission, review state, questions, objections, deadlines, approval conditions, and effective date.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Launch Availability Matrix shows every state with approved versions, configuration readiness, earliest sale date, and launch decision.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Approved Rate Audit shows filed factors beside configured factors and flags version mismatches.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Regulatory Filing is coherent. Its output is Jurisdiction Authorized for Sale. We now move to Distribution and Sales.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain three is Distribution and Sales. Events first, from a sellable product to a completed application.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Product Offered to Channel, Producer Authorized to Sell, Prospect Created, and Lead Assigned.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Then Application Started, Applicant Identified, Business Location Added, Business Operations Described, and Coverage Preferences Captured.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Data Retrieval Consent Granted or Data Retrieval Consent Declined must be explicit events.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: The sales sequence ends with Application Completed, Application Abandoned, or Application Withdrawn.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: A Distribution Manager issues Offer Product to Channel and Authorize Producer to Sell.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: An Agent, Customer, or Service Representative issues Create Prospect, Start Application, Identify Applicant, Add Business Location, Describe Business Operations, Select Coverage Preferences, and Complete Application.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Only the Applicant issues Grant Data Retrieval Consent or Decline Data Retrieval Consent.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Distribution and Sales hotspots.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Hotspot: agents say they own the application, while direct sales says the customer owns it.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Resolution: the Applicant owns attestations and consent. A Producer or Service Representative may prepare data but cannot attest without documented authority.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Hotspot: one business may have duplicate prospects from direct and agency channels.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Resolution: Prospect is channel-specific, while Applicant Identity is matched separately using legal entity identifiers without silently merging active applications.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Distribution and Sales policies and invariants.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Policy: whenever an application requests third-party data, verify Data Retrieval Consent Granted and that the data source is permitted in the jurisdiction.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Policy: whenever an application is inactive for seven days, send a reminder; after thirty days, emit Application Abandoned.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Invariant: an Application Completed event references one Applicant, one product and jurisdiction, one requested effective date, and all required attestations.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Distribution and Sales screens.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Sales Funnel shows prospects, applications, completion rate, source, producer, stage age, abandonment reason, and conversion.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Application Workspace shows sections, completion status, validation issues, consent, collaborators, and requested coverage.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Producer Authority View shows license, appointment, product authorization, jurisdiction, effective dates, and restrictions.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Distribution and Sales is coherent. Its output is Application Completed. We now move to Underwriting and Quoting.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain four is Underwriting and Quoting. Events first, beginning with a completed application.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Risk Data Requested, Risk Data Received, Risk Data Incomplete, and Exposure Estimated.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Then Appetite Evaluated, Risk Eligible, Risk Referred, or Risk Declined.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: For referred risks: Underwriting Referral Created, Additional Information Requested, Additional Information Received, Subjectivity Added, Subjectivity Satisfied, and Risk Approved with Terms.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: For approved risks: Premium Calculated, Quote Generated, Quote Offered, Quote Revised, Quote Expired, Quote Accepted, or Quote Declined.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: The system issues Gather Risk Data using approved external providers such as business registry, geocoding, catastrophe score, and prior-loss exchange.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: The Underwriting Decision Service issues Evaluate Appetite. An Underwriter issues Request Additional Information, Add Subjectivity, Satisfy Subjectivity, Approve Risk with Terms, or Decline Risk.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: The Rating Service issues Calculate Premium. An Agent or Customer issues Generate Quote, Revise Quote, Accept Quote, or Decline Quote.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Underwriting and Quoting hotspots.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Hotspot: Risk Declined and Risk Referred are often conflated, which leads sales to tell customers they were declined while review is still possible.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: referral is a pending decision with an owner and due time; decline is a final underwriting decision for that application version.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Hotspot: agents want to edit a quote in place, but that destroys rating reproducibility.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Resolution: Quote is immutable. Revised inputs create a new Quote Version linked to a new reproducible Premium Calculation.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Hotspot: internal decline reasons may contain protected or fraud-sensitive information.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: Underwriting owns internal reasons; Communications maps them to approved customer-facing notices.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Underwriting and Quoting policies and invariants.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Policy: whenever Risk Referred, create a referral with authority level, evidence checklist, owner, and service deadline.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Policy: whenever required risk data is missing, emit Risk Data Incomplete and do not evaluate appetite.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Policy: whenever approved terms or rating inputs change, recalculate premium and generate a new quote version.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Invariant: every Quote Offered references one application version, underwriting decision, product version, approved rate version, rating inputs, premium result, terms, and expiration.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Underwriting and Quoting screens.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Underwriting Work Queue shows referrals, reason, authority required, missing evidence, subjectivities, owner, due time, and aging.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Risk Decision Workspace shows application facts, external data, rule outcomes, prior losses, decision history, and authority controls.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Quote Comparison shows quote versions, coverages, limits, deductibles, exclusions, premium, payment options, and expiration.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Underwriting and Quoting is coherent. Its output is Quote Accepted with all bind prerequisites visible. We now move to Binding and Policy Issuance.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain five is Binding and Policy Issuance. Events first.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Quote Accepted, Bind Requested, Electronic Consent Captured, Required Document Signed, and Bind Subjectivity Satisfied.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Billing Setup Requested, Billing Account Established, Down Payment Received, or Billing Setup Rejected.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Bind Readiness Evaluated, Bind Approved, or Bind Rejected.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Then Policy Number Reserved, Coverage Bound, Binder Generated, Policy Issued, Policy Package Assembled, Policy Package Delivered, or Document Delivery Failed.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: The Applicant issues Request Bind and Capture Electronic Consent. The Applicant or authorized Producer issues Sign Required Document.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Binding issues Establish Billing Account and Collect Down Payment according to the selected billing plan.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: The Binding Service issues Evaluate Bind Readiness and Bind Coverage.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Policy Administration issues Reserve Policy Number and Issue Policy. Documents issues Generate Binder, Assemble Policy Package, and Deliver Policy Package.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Binding and Issuance hotspots.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Hotspot: sales treats Quote Accepted as coverage, but required payment or subjectivities may still be open.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: only Coverage Bound means coverage exists. Quote Accepted creates a Bind Request, never coverage.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Hotspot: a document-generation failure after bind can look like a failed purchase.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Resolution: Coverage Bound is durable. Binder Generation Failed creates an operations exception and customer message but never reverses coverage.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Binding and Issuance policies and invariants.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Policy: Bind Approved only when quote is unexpired, terms unchanged, signatures complete, subjectivities satisfied, producer authorized, and billing prerequisites met.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Policy: whenever Coverage Bound, generate binder, issue policy, assemble package, and notify customer and producer.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Invariant: Bind Coverage is idempotent. Repeating the same bind request returns the same policy number and never creates duplicate coverage.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Invariant: Coverage Bound records legal timestamp, time zone, effective date, jurisdiction, accepted quote version, terms, and binding authority.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Binding and Issuance screens.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Bind Readiness Checklist shows every prerequisite, status, responsible party, evidence, and resolution action.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Issuance Exceptions Queue shows failed billing setup, duplicate requests, binder failures, policy issuance failures, and delivery failures.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Coverage Confirmation shows policy number, legal insured, effective date, bound terms, binder link, package status, and billing plan.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Binding and Policy Issuance is coherent. Its output is an active issued policy. We now move to Policy Servicing.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain six is Policy Servicing. Events first, focusing on customer and agent changes after issuance.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Service Request Created, Policy Change Requested, Change Evidence Received, and Change Effective Date Proposed.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Change Screened, Straight Through Change Eligible, Underwriting Review Required, Change Approved, or Change Declined.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Premium Change Calculated, Additional Premium Calculated, Return Premium Calculated, or No Premium Change.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Then Change Accepted, Policy Endorsed, Endorsement Document Generated, Billing Adjustment Posted, or Service Request Closed.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: For loss reporting, First Notice of Loss Captured and Claim Intake Referred are the only servicing events; Claims owns everything after referral.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: A Customer, Agent, or Service Representative issues Create Service Request, Request Policy Change, Provide Change Evidence, and Propose Change Effective Date.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: The Change Screening Service issues Screen Policy Change. An Underwriter issues Approve Policy Change or Decline Policy Change when review is required.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: The Rating Service issues Calculate Premium Change. The Customer or authorized Producer issues Accept Policy Change.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Policy Administration issues Apply Endorsement. Service issues Capture First Notice of Loss and Refer Claim Intake.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Policy Servicing hotspots.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Hotspot: staff use service request and endorsement interchangeably.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: Service Request is a work item. Endorsement is a legally effective policy version created only by Apply Endorsement.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Hotspot: backdated changes can create retroactive coverage or erase earned premium.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Resolution: change type and jurisdiction determine permitted effective-date authority; exceptions require underwriting and compliance approval.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Policy Servicing policies and invariants.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Policy: whenever Policy Change Requested, screen materiality, authority, evidence, and effective-date eligibility before rating.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Policy: whenever approved coverage or exposure changes, calculate premium change before the customer accepts.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Policy: whenever Policy Endorsed, generate endorsement documents, post billing adjustment, notify stakeholders, and close the request when all outputs succeed.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Invariant: policy versions are immutable and effective-dated. Every endorsement references one prior version and produces one new version.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Policy Servicing screens.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Service Work Queue shows request type, policy, customer, status, owner, missing evidence, due time, premium impact, and exceptions.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Policy Timeline shows bind, issuance, versions, endorsements, billing facts, documents, communications, and claim referrals while preserving each source of truth.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Agent Book of Business shows active policies, current terms, open service requests, renewals, documents, and commission-impacting changes.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Policy Servicing is coherent. Its output is a versioned, current policy and closed service work. We now move to Billing and Collections.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain seven is Billing and Collections. Events first.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Billing Account Established, Installment Schedule Created, Invoice Issued, Payment Scheduled, Payment Received, or Payment Failed.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Then Account Past Due, Delinquency Cured, Cancellation Notice Issued, Cancellation Pending, Cancellation Pending Withdrawn, or Policy Cancelled for Nonpayment.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: For recovery: Reinstatement Requested, No Loss Statement Received, Reinstatement Approved, Reinstatement Declined, and Policy Reinstated.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Billing issues Create Installment Schedule, Issue Invoice, Schedule Payment, Apply Payment, Mark Account Past Due, Issue Cancellation Notice, and Cancel Policy for Nonpayment.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: A Customer or Agent issues Make Payment and Request Reinstatement.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: The Customer issues Provide No Loss Statement. An authorized Underwriter issues Approve Reinstatement or Decline Reinstatement.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Policy Administration issues Reinstate Policy after approved terms and payment conditions are satisfied.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Billing and Collections hotspots.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Hotspot: staff say cancelled when they mean notice issued, cancellation pending, or actually cancelled.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: Notice Issued, Cancellation Pending, Cancelled, Withdrawn, and Reinstated remain distinct facts with effective timestamps.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Hotspot: a late invoice does not automatically authorize cancellation because notice periods, holidays, and proof of delivery vary by jurisdiction.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: a Compliance Calendar calculates the earliest legal cancellation date from policy, jurisdiction, reason, and delivery evidence.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Billing and Collections policies and invariants.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Policy: whenever Payment Failed and the grace threshold is exceeded, mark Account Past Due and issue the jurisdiction-approved notice.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Policy: whenever payment cures the full delinquency before cancellation, emit Delinquency Cured and withdraw cancellation pending.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Policy: reinstatement after the cancellation effective time requires payment resolution and any required no-loss or underwriting review.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Invariant: Policy Cancelled for Nonpayment cannot occur before the earliest legal date and verified notice delivery.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Billing and Collections screens.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Billing Account View shows balance, invoices, installments, payments, failures, fees, delinquency, notices, and cancellation timeline.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Collections Work Queue shows past-due accounts, legal deadlines, promised payments, notice status, exceptions, and cure amount.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Reinstatement Workspace shows cancellation facts, lapse period, payments, no-loss evidence, authority, decision, and reinstated terms.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Billing and Collections is coherent. Its output is an accurate account and truthful coverage status. We now move to Renewal and Retention.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Sub-domain eight is Renewal and Retention. Events first.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Renewal Review Scheduled, Renewal Review Started, Risk Data Refreshed, Material Change Detected, and Renewal Appetite Evaluated.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: The decision events are Renewal Eligible, Renewal Referred, Nonrenewal Proposed, and Nonrenewal Approved.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Then Renewal Premium Calculated, Renewal Offer Generated, Renewal Offered, Renewal Terms Revised, or Renewal Offer Expired.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: The customer outcome events are Renewal Accepted, Renewal Declined, Nonrenewal Notice Delivered, Policy Renewed, or Policy Expired without Renewal.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Events complete. Now commands and actors.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: The Renewal Scheduler issues Schedule Renewal Review and Start Renewal Review. Data services issue Refresh Risk Data.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Underwriting issues Evaluate Renewal Appetite, Refer Renewal, Propose Nonrenewal, Approve Nonrenewal, and Revise Renewal Terms.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Rating issues Calculate Renewal Premium. Policy Administration issues Generate Renewal Offer.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: A Customer or authorized Producer issues Accept Renewal or Decline Renewal. Policy Administration issues Renew Policy or Expire Policy without Renewal.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Renewal and Retention hotspots.

speaker: Noah (Actuarial)
text: Hotspot: teams disagree whether renewal uses the old policy's rates or current approved rates.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Resolution: renewal uses the product and approved rate versions effective on the new term date, while preserving prior-term values for comparison.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Hotspot: renewal offered is sometimes treated as automatically renewed.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Resolution: Renewal Offered is an offer. Policy Renewed occurs only after acceptance or legally supported automatic-renewal rules and required payment conditions.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Renewal and Retention policies and invariants.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Policy: whenever a policy enters its renewal review window, schedule review using product-specific lead time and jurisdictional notice requirements.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Policy: whenever Material Change Detected or renewal rules refer the risk, create a renewal referral with owner and deadline.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Policy: whenever Nonrenewal Approved, deliver the approved notice before the jurisdictional deadline and retain delivery evidence.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Invariant: Renew Policy is idempotent and creates exactly one new term linked to the expiring term.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Now Renewal and Retention screens.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Renewal Work Queue shows policies entering review, change indicators, referral reasons, owner, notice deadline, offer deadline, and outcome.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Renewal Proposal compares expiring and offered terms, premium, limits, deductibles, forms, reasons for change, and actions required.

speaker: Priya (Product)
text: Retention Dashboard shows eligible policies, offers, acceptances, nonrenewals, expirations, premium change, channel, segment, and reason codes.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Renewal and Retention is coherent. Its output is either a linked new policy term or a properly noticed expiration.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: Let us finish with the context map. Product Design publishes Product Design Approved to Regulatory Filing.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Regulatory Filing publishes Jurisdiction Authorized for Sale to Distribution, Underwriting, Rating, and Product Configuration.

speaker: Marcus (Distribution)
text: Distribution publishes Application Completed to Underwriting and receives Quote Offered, decline notices, and referral status.

speaker: Elena (Underwriting)
text: Underwriting publishes Risk Approved with Terms to Quoting and Bind Approved to Binding, without owning the long-lived Policy.

speaker: Tariq (Engineering)
text: Binding publishes Coverage Bound to Policy Administration, Billing, Documents, Communications, Distribution, and Analytics.

speaker: Sofia (Service)
text: Policy Administration owns policy versions; Servicing, Billing, and Renewal request controlled changes and consume authoritative policy facts.

speaker: Rina (Compliance)
text: Documents and Communications translate authoritative facts into approved artifacts and notices but never decide coverage or policy state.

speaker: Maya (Facilitator)
text: The model now progresses coherently through eight sub-domains. Each has explicit events, commands, actors, resolved hotspots, policies, invariants, screens, and a defined output contract to the next sub-domain.
